mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which signals economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of rising housing sales (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a single month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month AND UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market signals (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or decreasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), indicates strong consumer demand without inflationary pressure, which is conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases over 3 months AND CPIAUCSL stable or decreases
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong retail sales without inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a single month, coupled with an increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the previous quarter, signals accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.5% in 1 month AND GDPC1 increases > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of easing monetary policy with GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates a robust supply side and a strong labor market, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases over 3 months AND UNRATE stable or decreases
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing industrial production with stable or decreasing unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).
